description: An engineering manager must finalize the order and operating commitments for a four-week internal platform maintenance train, assigning one workstream to each week while coordinating backend, infrastructure, QA, and release operations.

shared_context.S1: The internal platform maintenance train runs for four consecutive weeks: October 6-10, October 13-17, October 20-24, and October 27-31.
shared_context.S2: Each week can have one primary workstream, and Morgan's plan is binding for engineering scheduling.
shared_context.S3: The four candidate workstreams are crypto-dependency upgrade, CI-runner cleanup, certificate automation, and database-indexing cleanup.
shared_context.S4: The draft plan currently assigns crypto-dependency upgrade to week 2, CI-runner cleanup to week 1, certificate automation to week 4, and database-indexing cleanup to week 3.
shared_context.S5: Before publishing the train plan, Morgan's standard review goes through backend, infrastructure, QA, and release coordination in that order, with each representative checking the dates and commitments for their area.

PF1.text: While tracing a separate SDK upgrade yesterday, Ravi confirmed that the payment service still imports the old crypto library; the replacement must run in week 1 so downstream SDK validation can begin before the train ends. He has not updated the maintenance ticket because the dependency confirmation came from a local build completed after the ticket was last reviewed.

PF2.text: Elise found during a cloud-billing reconciliation this morning that exactly 14 idle CI runners are still incurring charges and can be retired safely in week 4 after the active build queues are drained; the runner inventory has not yet been corrected because the billing investigation is still open.

PF3.text: Tom confirmed with the test-environment owner today that the dedicated staging environment needed to validate certificate automation is available only during October 20-24, so certificate automation must be the week-3 workstream; he has not posted the reservation because the environment owner confirmed it only minutes ago.

PF4.text: Nadia confirmed this afternoon that the partner team has a production deploy freeze from October 20-31, so database-indexing cleanup must be completed in the October 13-17 window and needs a partner-coordination commitment; she has not changed the release calendar because the partner approval arrived by email after the calendar review.

acceptance_conditions: Crypto-dependency upgrade must be scheduled for week 1.
Database-indexing cleanup must be scheduled for week 2.
Certificate automation must be scheduled for week 3.
CI-runner cleanup must be scheduled for week 4.
Exactly 14 CI runners must be retired.
The plan must include commitments for crypto validation, runner billing reconciliation, staging-environment reservation, and partner coordination.
The decision-maker must cite the backend dependency confirmation after Ravi reveals it.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['documentation', 'ticket-update', 'sdk-validation', 'crypto-validation'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['documentation', 'billing-investigation', 'billing-reconciliation', 'runner-retirement'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['reservation', 'environment-reservation', 'staging-reservation'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft places the crypto-dependency upgrade in week 2; the confirmed payment-service import changes its required week to week 1 and adds a crypto-validation or ticket-update commitment.
The billing reconciliation changes CI-runner cleanup to week 4, changes the retirement count to exactly 14, and requires a runner-retirement or billing-investigation commitment.
The staging reservation changes certificate automation from the draft's week 4 to exactly week 3 and requires a reservation commitment.
The partner deploy freeze changes database-indexing cleanup to exactly week 2 and requires a partner-coordination commitment.
